title: ESO Guideline 2024: Diagnosis and Management of Patent Foramen Ovale After Stroke

recommendations.text: High-quality evidence supports PFO closure plus antiplatelet therapy in selected patients aged 18-60 years in whom no other evident cause of stroke is found. The PASCAL classification can be used to select candidates; patients with both a large right-to-left shunt and an atrial septal aneurysm benefit most.
There is insufficient evidence for an evidence-based recommendation on PFO closure in patients older than 60 or younger than 18 years.
Low-quality evidence suggests against PFO closure in patients whose stroke is unlikely PFO-related by PASCAL classification, except in specific scenarios.
ESO suggests against long-term anticoagulation in PFO-associated stroke unless anticoagulation is indicated for other medical reasons.

The working group notes an evidentiary gap in the diagnostic algorithm for PFO detection; transoesophageal echocardiography is conventionally held as most accurate but its 'gold standard' status is not substantiated by rigorously validated evidence.
